description: Where each Jetpack Settings hash route and ?term= search goes once the Settings screen retires. Nothing reads it yet: the redirect document that page=jetpack-settings and the page=jetpack forwarder (Jetpack_React_Page) will print resolves these rules in PHP, since the server never sees the hash. It applies only while Initializer::is_settings_consolidation_enabled() is true. The Network Admin jetpack-settings page is out of scope. It is production-excluded in .gitattributes; the PR that first reads it must remove that exclusion.
matching: `everySource` runs before any route or term rule. A term matches its decoded value, case-insensitively, before its route; an unmatched term falls back to its route. On page=jetpack-settings, an empty hash (the bare menu link) or an unknown route gets the /settings rules, as main.jsx does. On page=jetpack, an unknown route never reaches these rules: the forwarder (Jetpack_React_Page::get_legacy_route_redirects()) sends it to My Jetpack for admins and to Settings for everyone else, as it does today, so #/my-plan, #/dashboard and #/stats keep landing on My Jetpack. In each list, the first rule whose `when` all hold wins, and a rule without `when` is the default. A rule with `pending` keeps the source on Settings until each marker clears: `D<n>` is an open decision, `JETPACK-<n>` an issue that must land, `flag:<name>` a feature flag that must retire, `error-notice-home` a new home for the Jetpack::state( 'error' ) notice, which only Settings shows today, and `monetize-page` a Monetize page that shows the Ads settings (its flag on and the `monetize` module active), without which the Ads settings stay on Settings. A `destination` next to `pending` is where the source goes once it clears. A settings panel destination (`configure=`) waits on the issue that gives the panel that module's settings, since until then the panel's fallback links back here through configure_url. Destinations are relative to wp-admin. My Jetpack `#/` links work on every My Jetpack version, since its router rewrites them to `?p=`.

decisions.D2: Whether Comments' settings (with Gravatar Hovercards and Markdown for comments) get one settings panel or become Features switches, and where the Markdown option goes.
decisions.D6: Where Reader Visibility goes (a Features switch, or Newsletter settings).
decisions.D7: Where Google Analytics settings go on Atomic (the SEO page, or Stats settings).
decisions.D9: Where users who cannot manage modules find Post by Email, Publicize and their own account connection, since Features needs manage_options.
decisions.D10: What happens to the legacy SEO block on self-hosted sites that have not opted in to the SEO page.
decisions.D11: Where the per-user usage tracking (Privacy) setting lives.

conditions.partnerCoupon: Jetpack_React_Page::get_partner_coupon_redirect() returns a URL; that screen takes every route.
conditions.error: Jetpack::state( 'error' ) is set. Settings is the only screen that shows it, so Jetpack_React_Page::should_redirect_legacy_routes() keeps the user there.
conditions.canManageModules: The user has jetpack_manage_modules. Users without it reach Settings only for Publicize and Post by Email.
conditions.adsSettingsHome: Jetpack_Ads_Settings_Home::is_moved_off_settings(): settings consolidation is on and the Monetize page shows the Ads settings.

moduleTerms: Every module slug below is also linked by Jetpack::module_configuration_url(), the Configure link in Features and the classic Modules list, unless the module filters that URL.
protectTerms: The waf, protect, account-protection, sso and monitor destinations copy Automattic\Jetpack\Protect\Dashboard::get_module_settings_urls(); call it rather than hard-coding them.
